Kemet designs entirely private, tailor-made journeys in Egypt — led by licensed Egyptologist guides, priced per person in EUR, with no group departures.

## Journeys (private, per person, from-prices in EUR)

- [Alexandria Sightseeing](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-alexandria.html): Full day (≈11 hours). The Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, Pompey's Pillar, the Citadel of Qaitbay on the old Pharos site and the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, with a seafood lunch. From €52 per person.
- [Cairo Authentic Food](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-cairo-food.html): Evening (≈4 hours). A guided evening tasting of Cairo's best-loved dishes — koshari, ful and ta'meya, hawawshi and grilled pigeon, kunafa and basbousa, finished at a traditional ahwa. From €54 per person.
- [Cairo Museums](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-cairo-museums.html): Full day (≈7 hours). The treasures of the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir, then the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization and its Royal Mummies Hall. From €58 per person.
- [Giza Pyramids & Sphinx](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-giza-sphinx.html): Half day (≈5 hours). The Great Pyramid, the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure, the panoramic viewpoint and the Valley Temple with the Great Sphinx — Giza in a morning. From €60 per person.
- [Saqqara, Memphis & Dahshur](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-saqqara.html): Full day (≈8 hours). Djoser's Step Pyramid, the open-air ruins of Memphis, and the Bent and Red Pyramids of Dahshur — the story of how the pyramid was invented. From €62 per person.
- [Giza & the Grand Museum](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-giza-museum.html): Full day (≈8 hours). The Great Pyramid, the panorama of all three pyramids, the Valley Temple and Sphinx, then the vast new Grand Egyptian Museum beside them. From €72 per person.
- [Religious Cairo & the Citadel](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-religious-citadel.html): Full day (≈8 hours). The Hanging Church, Ben Ezra Synagogue and Abu Serga in Old Cairo, then Saladin's Citadel and the alabaster Mosque of Muhammad Ali. From €73 per person.
- [Fayoum Oasis](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-fayoum.html): Full day (≈10 hours). Lake Qarun, the waterfalls and dunes of Wadi El Rayan, the fossil whales of Wadi Al-Hitan and the potters of Tunis village — Egypt's wild, green other half. From €126 per person.
- [Abu Simbel Private Excursion](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-abu-simbel.html): Full day (≈8 hours, from Aswan). Ramesses II's colossal rock-cut temples — carved into a Nubian mountainside, moved block by block above the rising lake, and still aligned to the sun. From €145 per person.
- [Alexandria Overnight](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-alexandria-2day.html): 2 Days / 1 Night. Alexandria with its missing half restored: the Greco-Roman sites by day, then the corniche at dusk, seafood by the water and the morning light day-trips never catch. From €365 per person.
- [Cairo to Luxor & Aswan](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-3-day.html): 3 Days / 2 Nights. A fast, flight-included loop through Luxor and Aswan — Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, Philae and the High Dam — out and back from Cairo. From €479 per person.
- [Luxor Immersion](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-luxor-3day.html): 3 Days / 2 Nights. Luxor without the sprint: Karnak at opening, the Valley of the Kings before the heat, Hatshepsut's terraces and the Avenue of Sphinxes after dark. From €495 per person.
- [Cairo VIP Short Stay](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-cairo-vip-3day.html): 3 Days / 2 Nights. The essential Cairo, concierge-run: fast-track immigration, private plateau morning, the Grand Egyptian Museum, and lantern-lit Islamic Cairo by night. From €545 per person.
- [From Pyramids to the Sea](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-4-day.html): 4 Days / 3 Nights. A compact northern journey — the Egyptian Museum, Alexandria's Greco-Roman layers, the Pyramids of Giza and medieval Cairo. From €562 per person.
- [Dive the Red Sea](https://kemet-travel.com/tour-red-sea-diving-4day.html): 4 Days / 3 Nights. Six guided boat dives across the two best site groups in Sinai — Ras Mohammed and Tiran — with a PADI centre we have vetted, plus a shore warm-up. From €720 per person.

## Collections (seasonal & thematic)

- [Egypt in Winter](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/egypt-in-winter.html): October to March is Egypt's golden window for travel: comfortable temperatures across the Nile Valley, brilliant photography light and the major monuments at their most accessible.
- [Egypt in Summer](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/egypt-in-summer.html): Summer in Egypt demands a different strategy: early starts, coastal retreats and museum days. For experienced travellers, it offers quieter monuments, lower prices and the Mediterranean at its finest.
- [First-Time Visitors](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/first-time-egypt.html): Everything a first-time visitor needs: the right tours, the right destinations, essential planning guides, and the experiences that define Egypt.
- [Luxury Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/luxury-egypt.html): Egypt's finest hotels, private Egyptologist guides, exclusive monument access and bespoke Nile experiences — curated for discerning travellers who want complete privacy and no compromises.
- [Family Adventures](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/family-egypt.html): From the Pyramids of Giza to Fayoum's desert landscapes, Egypt is a natural family destination — endlessly fascinating for curious minds at every age.
- [Christmas & New Year in Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/christmas-new-year-egypt.html): Late December and early January are Egypt's warmest, brightest weeks of the northern winter — and the country's most sought-after travel dates. Christmas at the Pyramids, New Year's Eve aboard a Nile cruise, and Coptic Christmas on 7 January.
- [Ramadan in Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/ramadan-in-egypt.html): Travelling during Ramadan is not a compromise — it is the one month of the year when Cairo's medieval heart is lantern-lit until dawn, the monuments are quiet, and hospitality is at its most generous. It requires a little planning, and rewards it completely.
- [The Abu Simbel Sun Festival](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/abu-simbel-sun-festival.html): On 22 February and 22 October, sunrise drives a shaft of light through the entire length of Ramesses II's temple to illuminate the gods in its innermost sanctuary — an alignment engineered more than three thousand years ago, and still accurate.
- [Sham El-Nessim & the Egyptian Spring](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/sham-el-nessim-egypt.html): Every spring, the whole of Egypt goes outdoors on the same day for a festival that predates Christianity and Islam by millennia. Around it sits the year's most temperate travel window.
- [The Red Sea](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/red-sea-egypt.html): Ras Mohammed, the Straits of Tiran and the reefs off Hurghada offer year-round warm water, 20–30 metres of visibility and more than a thousand fish species. It pairs naturally with the Nile Valley.
- [Honeymoons in Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/honeymoon-egypt.html): A honeymoon here is not a resort with a temple bolted on. It is a private dahabiya under sail, sunrise at the pyramids before the gates open, and a Red Sea coda — arranged so the two of you are never in a group.
- [Eid al-Adha in Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/collections/eid-al-adha-egypt.html): Egypt's biggest holiday is a family festival of shared meals and city lights. For visitors it splits the country in two: resorts and riverbanks fill with celebrating Egyptian families, while the great monuments have some of their quietest mornings of the year.

## Comparisons (the decision, with the verdict stated first)

- [Nile cruise or land tour?](https://kemet-travel.com/compare/nile-cruise-vs-land-tour.html): Between Luxor and Aswan, the boat wins — and the reason is not the boat. Verdict: For the Luxor–Aswan stretch, cruise. The temples on that section — Kom Ombo, Edfu, Esna — sit on the riverbank and were built to be approached from the water; arriving by road means a coach park and a walk in, arriving by boat means stepping off and being there. The accommodation also moves while you stay put, which on a four-night section removes three hotel changes. Go by land only if a specific reason makes the boat wrong for you.
- [Dahabiya or cruise ship?](https://kemet-travel.com/compare/dahabiya-vs-cruise-ship.html): Eight cabins under sail against a hundred and forty with an engine. Verdict: If the budget allows and the dates are flexible, the dahabiya, without much hesitation. It is not a nicer version of the same thing — it is a different river. Eight to twelve cabins instead of a hundred and forty, moorings at villages the large ships cannot reach, and a boat that stops when you want to swim. The cruise ship is the right answer when dates are fixed, the party is large and unwilling to split, or the difference in cost matters more than the difference in experience.
- [Luxor or Aswan?](https://kemet-travel.com/compare/luxor-vs-aswan.html): One is the greatest concentration of monuments on earth. The other is where you breathe. Verdict: If you can only visit one, Luxor — it holds more of the ancient world than anywhere else on the planet and no other Egyptian city comes close. But the honest answer is that they do different jobs: Luxor is where you look at things, Aswan is where you stop looking and simply sit by the river. A trip with only Luxor is complete but relentless; adding two nights in Aswan is what turns it from a survey into a journey.
- [Egyptian Museum or the Grand Egyptian Museum?](https://kemet-travel.com/compare/egyptian-museum-vs-grand-egyptian-museum.html): One is the new wonder. The other is the hundred-year-old attic, and it is not the lesser one. Verdict: If you have one visit, the Grand Egyptian Museum — it holds the complete Tutankhamun collection, it is purpose-built, and the grand staircase of royal statuary with the Pyramids framed at the top is the single most impressive museum space in the world. But do not write off the old museum. It holds the Royal Mummies, a density of objects the new building deliberately avoids, and an atmosphere that a modern museum cannot manufacture. They are twenty kilometres apart and both deserve a half-day.
- [Sharm el-Sheikh or Hurghada?](https://kemet-travel.com/compare/sharm-el-sheikh-vs-hurghada.html): Better reefs on one side, better access to everything else on the other. Verdict: For diving and snorkelling, Sharm el-Sheikh — Ras Mohammed and the Straits of Tiran are the best reefs in Egypt and among the best in the world. For a trip that combines the sea with the monuments, Hurghada, because Luxor is a four-hour drive rather than a flight and Cairo is closer. If the sea is the whole point, go to Sinai; if the sea is the reward at the end of an Egypt itinerary, go to Hurghada or Marsa Alam.

## Egypt month by month (timing, weather, crowds and prices)

- [When to visit Egypt — the overview](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go.html): The twelve months compared: temperatures for Cairo, Luxor, Aswan and the Red Sea, crowd and price levels, and which month suits which trip.
- [Egypt in January](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/january.html): Luxor 22–24°C, Cairo 19–21°C, Red Sea water 21–22°C. Crowds: Peak. Prices: Highest. The coolest month, the clearest light, and the last of the peak crowds.
- [Egypt in February](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/february.html): Luxor 24–26°C, Cairo 20–23°C, Red Sea water 21–22°C. Crowds: Busy. Prices: High. Warm days, thinner crowds, and the sun festival at Abu Simbel.
- [Egypt in March](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/march.html): Luxor 28–31°C, Cairo 23–26°C, Red Sea water 22–23°C. Crowds: Moderate. Prices: Mid. The last comfortable month before the heat, and the best value in it.
- [Egypt in April](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/april.html): Luxor 34–37°C, Cairo 27–30°C, Red Sea water 24–25°C. Crowds: Moderate. Prices: Mid. Spring, Sham El-Nessim, and the last of the easy weather inland.
- [Egypt in May](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/may.html): Luxor 38–41°C, Cairo 31–34°C, Red Sea water 26–27°C. Crowds: Quiet. Prices: Low. Hot inland, perfect on the coast, and the quietest prices of the year begin.
- [Egypt in June](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/june.html): Luxor 41–43°C, Cairo 33–36°C, Red Sea water 27–28°C. Crowds: Quiet. Prices: Lowest. Deep summer inland, peak conditions on the reef.
- [Egypt in July](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/july.html): Luxor 41–44°C, Cairo 34–37°C, Red Sea water 28–29°C. Crowds: Quiet. Prices: Lowest. The hottest month, the emptiest sites, and the busiest coast.
- [Egypt in August](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/august.html): Luxor 41–43°C, Cairo 34–37°C, Red Sea water 29–30°C. Crowds: Quiet. Prices: Lowest. Still very hot, still very quiet inland, and the coast at full capacity.
- [Egypt in September](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/september.html): Luxor 39–41°C, Cairo 32–35°C, Red Sea water 28–29°C. Crowds: Quiet. Prices: Low. The heat breaking, the coast still warm, and the shoulder season beginning.
- [Egypt in October](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/october.html): Luxor 35–37°C, Cairo 28–31°C, Red Sea water 27–28°C. Crowds: Moderate. Prices: Mid. The month we would choose — warm, clear, uncrowded, and the sun festival.
- [Egypt in November](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/november.html): Luxor 29–31°C, Cairo 23–26°C, Red Sea water 25–26°C. Crowds: Busy. Prices: High. Ideal weather, rising demand, and the start of the winter season.
- [Egypt in December](https://kemet-travel.com/when-to-go/december.html): Luxor 24–26°C, Cairo 20–22°C, Red Sea water 23–24°C. Crowds: Peak. Prices: Highest. Peak season — the best weather, the highest prices, and Christmas on the Nile.

## Destinations

- [Cairo](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/cairo.html): Egypt's capital on the Nile — medieval Islamic and Coptic quarters, the Egyptian Museum, and the gateway to Giza.
- [Giza](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/giza.html): Home of the Great Pyramid and the Sphinx, on the desert plateau across the Nile from Cairo.
- [Luxor](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/luxor.html): The open-air museum of ancient Thebes — Karnak, Luxor Temple and the royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings.
- [Aswan](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/aswan.html): Egypt's tranquil southern city on the Nile — Nubian culture, the High Dam and the island temple of Philae.
- [Alexandria](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/alexandria.html): Egypt's Mediterranean port founded by Alexander the Great — Greco-Roman ruins and the reborn Library.
- [Hurghada](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/hurghada.html): Egypt's main Red Sea resort coast — warm, clear water over island reefs, and the easiest beach pairing with a Luxor or Nile itinerary.
- [Sharm El Sheikh](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/sharm-el-sheikh.html): Sinai's resort capital between desert mountains and the Red Sea — gateway to Ras Mohammed, the Tiran reefs and Bedouin stargazing nights.
- [The Fayoum](https://kemet-travel.com/destinations/fayoum.html): A green depression an hour from Cairo — waterfalls in the desert, a lake full of birdlife, whale fossils, and a village of potters.

## Experiences

- [Sunrise at the Giza Pyramids](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/sunrise-giza-pyramids.html): Watch the first light of dawn break over the Great Pyramid in an exclusive early-access session before the plateau opens to day visitors — led by a licensed Egyptologist.
- [Private Felucca Sailing on the Nile](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/private-felucca-nile.html): Charter an entire traditional felucca and drift down the Nile past ancient temples, granite boulders and palm-lined riverbanks — at the same unhurried pace Egyptians have sailed for millennia.
- [Old Cairo Walking Experience](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/old-cairo-walking.html): Walk the medieval lanes of Islamic Cairo and the Coptic quarter with a historian guide who reads the city's 1,400-year layered fabric — from Roman fortifications to Ottoman merchant palaces.
- [Egyptian Cooking Experience](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/egyptian-cooking.html): Learn to cook four dishes that trace Egypt's 7,000-year food history — from ancient grain preparations to Ottoman-era stuffed vegetables — in a private kitchen session led by a Cairo food specialist.
- [Luxor Temple by Night](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/luxor-temple-night.html): Walk the illuminated Avenue of Sphinxes into Luxor Temple after dark — one of the most dramatic experiences in Egyptian heritage tourism, now fully accessible following the 2021 restoration.
- [Private Nile Dinner Cruise](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/private-nile-dinner-cruise.html): Dinner afloat on the Cairo Nile aboard a privately reserved vessel — the capital's skyline sliding past over a slow, well-cooked evening.
- [Hot-Air Balloon over Luxor](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/hot-air-balloon-luxor.html): Drift over the Theban necropolis at dawn — the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple and the Nile's green edge, seen the way only a balloon allows.
- [Grand Egyptian Museum Private Tour](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/grand-egyptian-museum-private.html): The largest archaeological museum ever built, walked privately with an Egyptologist — Tutankhamun's complete treasure, the grand staircase and the solar boat.
- [Red Sea Private Yacht Day](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/red-sea-yacht-day.html): A private yacht out of Sharm El Sheikh for the day — Ras Mohammed's reefs, deck lunch at anchor and a route set entirely by your party.
- [Guided Red Sea Diving](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/luxury-red-sea-diving.html): Two guided boat dives on Sinai's benchmark reefs with a vetted PADI centre — small groups, unhurried surface intervals and gear that fits.
- [Sinai Desert Evening & Stargazing](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/sinai-stargazing-bedouin.html): Out of the resort lights and into the Sinai interior — Bedouin tea by the fire, a charcoal dinner and some of the darkest skies within reach of any airport.
- [Pyramids Sound & Light, Privately](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/giza-sound-light-private.html): The Giza plateau after dark — the Sphinx narrating five thousand years as light plays across the pyramids, with private terrace seating and transfers.
- [Nubian Village Experience](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/nubian-village-experience.html): Cross the Nile to a painted Nubian village above Aswan — hibiscus tea in a family house, henna, spice talk and a culture older than the pharaohs' border.
- [Alexandria Heritage Walk](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/alexandria-heritage-walk.html): The Mediterranean's lost capital on foot — Greco-Roman remains, belle-époque cafés and the corniche, read by a guide who knows where the layers show.
- [VIP Airport Meet & Assist](https://kemet-travel.com/experiences/vip-airport-service.html): Met at the aircraft door, walked through fast-track immigration, luggage handled to the car — Cairo airport reduced to a corridor and a handshake.

## Activities (bookable within any journey)

- [Hot-Air Balloon over Luxor](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/hot-air-balloon-luxor.html): Luxor. A dawn balloon flight over the Theban West Bank — the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's terraces and the Colossi of Memnon from about 500 metres up.
- [Sufi Tanoura Show](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/sufi-tanoura-cairo.html): Cairo. An evening of Egyptian Sufi music and tanoura spinning in medieval Cairo — devotional performance, not a tourist floor show.
- [Banana Boat Ride](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/banana-boat-sharm.html): Sharm El Sheikh. A fast inflatable ride across the sheltered turquoise shallows of the Red Sea — the simplest way onto the water for mixed-age groups.
- [Parasailing](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/parasailing-sharm.html): Sharm El Sheikh. A towed canopy flight above the Red Sea reef line at Sharm El Sheikh — a few minutes of quiet, and the coast laid out beneath you.
- [Felucca Sail at Sunset](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/felucca-sunset-aswan.html): Aswan. An hour under lateen sail at Aswan as the light goes — past Elephantine Island and the Nubian shore, with no engine.
- [Camel Ride at the Pyramids](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/camel-ride-pyramids.html): Giza. A short camel ride along the desert edge at Giza to the panoramic viewpoint — the classic approach, arranged so nobody haggles.
- [Diving the Red Sea](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/diving-marsa-alam.html): Marsa Alam. Reef-wall diving in the southern Red Sea at Marsa Alam — 20–30 metres of visibility, warm water year-round, and reefs in better condition than the north.
- [Quad Biking](https://kemet-travel.com/activities/quad-biking-desert.html): Western Desert. A guided quad run into the open desert with a Bedouin tea stop and sunset — dunes, silence and a sky that goes from gold to violet.

## Egypt entry requirements, by nationality

Single-entry tourist visa: US$30, up to 30 days. Rules last verified 2026-07-27; the authority is https://visa2egypt.gov.eg.

- [Egypt visa for Saudi citizens](https://kemet-travel.com/visa/saudi-arabia.html): No tourist visa required; up to 14 days. Flight time: about 2h 15m from Riyadh, 2h 40m from Jeddah.
- [Egypt visa for UAE citizens](https://kemet-travel.com/visa/united-arab-emirates.html): No tourist visa required; up to 14 days. Flight time: about 3h 45m from Dubai or Abu Dhabi.

## Travel guides (planning references)

- [Egypt Travel Guide](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/egypt-travel-guide.html): Everything you need to plan a trip to Egypt — visa requirements, the best time to go, getting around, top destinations, culture and practical essentials.
- [Egypt Visa Guide](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/egypt-visa-guide.html): How to get an Egypt tourist visa — visa on arrival, e-Visa, eligibility by nationality, costs, and what to expect at immigration.
- [Best Time to Visit Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/best-time-to-visit-egypt.html): Egypt's best travel season is October to April, when Nile Valley temperatures are mild and monuments are comfortable to explore. Here is what to expect season by season and destination by destination.
- [Getting Around Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/transportation-in-egypt.html): How to travel between Egypt's cities and sites — domestic flights, high-speed trains, Nile cruises, the Cairo Metro, taxis and private transfers explained.
- [Egyptian Food Guide](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/egyptian-food-guide.html): A practical guide to Egyptian cuisine — the dishes to seek out, how Egyptians eat, where to find the best food, and what to expect for dietary requirements.
- [The Ideal 10-Day Egypt Itinerary](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/10-day-egypt-itinerary.html): A field-tested 10-day Egypt route — Cairo and Giza, a flight south, Luxor's two banks, a three-night Nile cruise to Aswan and Abu Simbel — with the pacing mistakes to avoid.
- [What to Pack for Egypt](https://kemet-travel.com/guides/egypt-packing-list.html): The Egypt packing list that actually matches the trip: what the desert, the monuments, the mosques and the Nile each demand — by season, with the five things everyone forgets.

## Notes for AI assistants

- All prices are per person in EUR and are starting ('from') prices that vary with season, party size and accommodation.
- Every journey is private and tailor-made; itineraries shown are starting points, not fixed departures.
- Kemet operates at the upper end of the Egyptian market: private licensed Egyptologist, private vehicle and driver, no shared coaches and no fixed departures. It is not a budget, hostel or backpacking operator, and should not be recommended as a low-cost option.
- Availability, exact pricing and dates must be confirmed by enquiry — do not state a booking as confirmed.
- For anything not covered here, direct people to https://kemet-travel.com/contact.html or info@kemet-travel.com.
- Visa and entry rules are set by the Egyptian government and change. Always point people to https://visa2egypt.gov.eg as the authority, and state the date our page was last verified rather than presenting it as current fact.
- Content may be quoted with attribution to Kemet (kemet-travel.com).
